item.title: Brussels blocks national social media age limits for 12 months pending EU-wide rules
item.description: The Commission's Kids Act sets 15 as the minimum age for opening an account across the EU, but Greece and Denmark say they will not wait. Austria will keep its own law ready to take effect when the standstill expires in July 2027.

item.title: Russia quits Europe's torture prevention treaty, ending detention monitoring in Russia
item.description: The withdrawal took effect one year after notification, and no independent body can now inspect Russian places of detention. The Council of Europe says the CPT will continue its work in the 46 remaining member states.

item.title: Sport court orders ice hockey federation to readmit Russia for 2027 worlds
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport found only substantiated security concerns can exclude athletes by nationality. Finland says Russian athletes will have no business coming to Finland, and the EU is weighing an entry ban for the Germany tournament.

item.title: Ukraine takes initiative on three fronts, ISW says, as Russian October losses hit record
item.description: Kyiv says more than 54,000 Russian soldiers were killed or seriously wounded in October, the highest toll since the 2022 invasion began. ISW says Ukraine seized the initiative in three directions and defeated Russia's northern pincer plan.

item.title: Coalition of the Willing holds first exercise in Poland from 9 to 22 November
item.description: RMF FM reports nearly 5,000 soldiers taking part, joined by British, French and limited German forces, to test the command and logistics systems needed to move troops across Europe. The United States is not taking part, and in July Russia's ambassador called the drills symbolic.

item.title: Hackers send false missile and nuclear alerts to Kyiv and all Russia in one night
item.description: Ukraine's Air Alert app and Russia's Emergency Ministry app were breached hours apart, and both governments restored their systems and denied any real threat. A previously unknown group, Hitcore, claimed the Ukrainian breach.

item.title: Two sanctions in one year, all against one broadcaster, are politics
item.description: The Media Authority warned, fined and threatened Ongehoord Nederland for a year before acting. When Zembla and BNNVARA broke the rules, it stayed silent, and that is what destroys a regulator.

item.title: Water cannon answers the riot. Only a budget answers the protest.
item.description: France and Germany met a generation's demands with 70,000 police and prosecutors' circulars, and nothing else. A state that can only repress, not respond, will keep repressing.

item.title: A union that outsources its border doesn't have one
item.description: The Council majority calls a bigger Frontex unnecessary while returns still depend on deals that can collapse with one election abroad. Build the 30,000-strong corps properly, write the safeguards in, and stop pretending the border works.

item.title: Poland's twenty-year EU ledger meets a budget that prices the border, not the balance
item.description: Poland enters the 2028-2034 budget talks with the union's strongest growth record and a fiscal bill of its own. The negotiating box measures it by Russia and Belarus instead, so the argument over what membership built is now the argument over what it gets.

item.title: Russian refinery damage lasts as long as the West keeps the repair parts banned
item.description: The strikes have taken half of Russia's refining capacity offline, yet exports rose to 7.7 million barrels a day. What decides whether the damage holds is not the number of drones but the export rules on secondary processing equipment, and those are held in Brussels and Washington.

item.title: Attal pushes open primary to block a Le Pen and Melanchon run-off in 2027
item.description: Marcangeli and Retailleau reject the plan as incoherent while Lisnard backs it. An Ipsos poll has Attal rising and Le Pen slipping, but her 33.5% still leads the field.

item.title: Russian man charged with espionage over train photos in Świdnica
item.description: Prosecutors found several hundred thousand files of railway and telecoms infrastructure on the man's devices, in a case officials link to wider Russian sabotage. In Warsaw, the president cut short a foreign trip after riot police blocked the Constitutional Tribunal.

item.title: Frankfurt riots injure more than 100 police as Hesse promises firmer response
item.description: Interior Minister Poseck did not rule out banning further assemblies after the looting of shops on the Zeil, while Mayor Josef refused his account of the suspects' origins.

item.title: Commission opens consultation on draft rule for AI Act penalty proceedings
item.description: The four-week consultation on the 10-page draft closes on 9 November 2026, with fines of up to 35 million euros or 7% of worldwide turnover at stake. Eight organisations have filed submissions so far.

item.title: France arrests 565 as youth protests turn violent in Germany and France
item.description: German organisers said 120,000 joined demos, below the 180,000 expected, after Frankfurt and Berlin saw riots, looting and injured police. Ministers blame extremist infiltrators; the movement disowns them.

item.title: Student unions call to block schools after police ban Paris demonstration route
item.description: Education minister Philippe Baptiste rejects the blockade and offers 1 billion euros for building renovations, while five unions have called an intersectoral strike for Thursday 5 November.

item.title: Russia vetoes US draft as UN mission in Western Sahara expires on 31 October
item.description: The Security Council failed to renew MINURSO's mandate for the first time, after Moscow blocked an American text that would have extended the mission to 2027 and removed its referendum role.

item.title: Ukrainian soldiers expect major Russian assault on Kherson as ceasefire ends on 1 Nov
item.description: Soldiers report KamAZ lorries moving combat units non-stop and Grad launchers massing near Radensk during the 80-hour truce, with the deputy governor warning of far heavier shelling from Monday. A civilian evacuation of about 2,000 residents in Oleshky begins Saturday.

item.title: CMPorts overtakes COSCO as Europe counts Chinese stakes in its ports
item.description: A study for the European Parliament put Chinese control at about 10% of European container throughput, and the two leading firms answer to the same state.
